subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes, or represent durable-write policy through enriched before_tool_call/provenance contracts instead?
rationale: The choice defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what plugins can see, whether they can block or mutate writes, and how failures affect durable data.

options.title: Design dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Enrich existing policy hooks
options.body: Extend before_tool_call and provenance context instead of adding a hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to provenance architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of persistent-state provenance work until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest hook-contract and adjacent operator-policy history among the likely owners.
